subject: DPA clarifications and data handling follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Gupta <aisha.gupta@stellarfinance.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA clarifications and next steps

Hi Aisha / Raj  

Thanks again for the productive discovery call today. Per our conversation, below is a concise recap of the data handling and privacy items you asked us to confirm, plus next steps: 

1) Controller / Processor: Redwood acts as a processor on behalf of Stellar Finance; you (Stellar) are the controller for customer data collected via your integration. We can reflect that language in the DPA.

2) Subprocessors: We maintain a list of subprocessors and provide notice prior to onboarding new subprocessors. I attached the baseline DPA (clean) and will send a tracked version with our proposed edits.

3) Data residency: For your EU customers we can pin inference and storage to our eu-west region in Dedicated/Private deployments. For hosted accounts we offer region scoping per contract.

4) Logging & retention: By default, request/response logs are retained for 30 days for troubleshooting; we offer configurable retention (including 0 retention) under contract for regulated workloads.

5) Breach notification: Our standard DPA commits to notifying customers without undue delay and, for incidents impacting customer data, we publish an incident report within 72 hours of confirming material impact. We can include more specific timelines in the DPA if needed.

Next steps:
- I attached the clean DPA for your legal team to review (Redwood_DPA_Clean.pdf).
- I'll follow up with a tracked-change DPA that addresses the items we discussed.
- Can we schedule a short meeting next week with your legal and security folks to walk through any redlines?

Thanks  

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0123

Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications and next steps

Thanks Marissa  

A few clarifying Qs from our side before we loop legal into formal redlines: 

- Controller/Processor: Can you confirm the DPA will explicitly state that Stellar Finance is the controller and Redwood is the processor, and that Redwood will follow controller instructions documented in the agreement?
- Subprocessors: We need the current subprocessor list and the notice window (we prefer 30 days) for new subprocessors. Do you publish the list publicly or provide it via a link?
- Breach notice timing: We require notification within 72 hours of discovery for incidents impacting customer data. Is that feasible for Redwood?
- Data residency: For certain workloads we need EU residency for both inference and stored transcripts. Will the hosted offering guarantee residency, or do we need Dedicated/Private?

Also, our legal team will likely submit a handful of redlines around indemnity and liability caps  

Best,
Aisha Gupta

Thanks  

Answered inline below and attached a tracked-changes DPA for legal (Stellar_DPA_Redwood_TrackChanges.docx).

- Controller/Processor: Yes  

we will state in Section 2 of the DPA that Stellar Finance is the controller and Redwood is the processor and that we will process data only on documented controller instructions. We can insert explicit language if your legal team requests it.

- Subprocessors: Our list is maintained on the link I shared (see related links). We provide advance notice prior to engaging any new subprocessor; our standard notice period is 30 days. We can negotiate longer notice in contract if required.

- Breach notice timing: Our internal incident response commits to notifying affected customers without undue delay; for incidents materially impacting customer data we aim to provide an initial notification within 72 hours of confirming the impact. We are willing to include the 72-hour language in the DPA where feasible.

- Data residency: For strict EU residency (inference + storage) we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment. For hosted we can scope customers to the EU region for inference, but transcript storage may be in our region-specific buckets  

Attached: Stellar_DPA_Redwood_TrackChanges.docx (tracked edits addressing controller/processor language, subprocessor notice, and proposed breach-notice clause).
